says: A REG file silently ignores every write (set value, delete value, clear key, forget key clearance) whose key is outside the source subtree it was created for (empty subtree accepts all; otherwise the key must equal the subtree or lie under it, case-insensitively). An export into a REG file therefore contains only the policy path, and nothing in the other keys is reported as skipped. Write it as a rule of the REG block, beside the write-target rule.

explanation: Overstated for the chosen item's own value: line 350 calls setValue(elemKey, ...) with the element's key always; a value has no key of its own, so 'both go under the element's key unless the item or its list names another key' is false for it. Only the item's value-list entries (lines 351, 285-290) may use their own key or the list's default key. State: the item's value is always written under the element's key; the item's list entries use their own key, else the list's default key, else the element's key.

The sentence 'A product with no sub-products is met only by being listed' holds only for a plain entry. A version-range entry for a product with no sub-products is never met, even when the product is listed: line 385 is skipped for ranges and line 386 returns False. Say so, so a range entry on a childless product reads as never met.

'entries after the first hold fewer strings than the first requires' is false. Line 114 picks the shape from the first entry only: exactly one string gives a plain list (later entries need at least one string, read as l(0)); any other count (including zero, which fails at once) gives a name/value list where every entry needs at least two strings (l(0), l(1)). Extra strings are ignored, and a later entry with two strings is accepted when the first had three. State: a first entry with no quoted text is refused; with one string, a later entry with none is refused; with two or more strings, a later entry with fewer than two is refused.
